questions.q: What lights up the Moon so we can see it at night?
questions.fact: The Moon does not make its own light. It shines by reflecting sunlight.

questions.q: Which star is closest to Earth?
questions.fact: The Sun is a star, and it gives us light and warmth.

questions.q: What planet do we live on?
questions.fact: Earth is the only planet we know of that has living things.

questions.q: Which planet is famous for its big rings?
questions.fact: Saturn's rings are made mostly of pieces of ice.

questions.q: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
questions.fact: Mars looks red because its rocks have rust in them.

questions.q: What do astronauts wear outside their spaceship?
questions.fact: A space suit gives an astronaut air and keeps them comfortable in space.

questions.q: What do we call people who travel into space?
questions.fact: The first person in space was Yuri Gagarin in 1961.

questions.q: How many moons does Earth have?
questions.fact: Our Moon is about one quarter as wide as Earth.

questions.q: What is a ball of ice and dust with a glowing tail?
questions.fact: A comet's tail always points away from the Sun.

questions.q: What do you use to look at faraway stars?
questions.fact: A telescope collects light so faraway things look bigger and brighter.

questions.q: What do we call a space robot that rolls around on Mars?
questions.fact: Rovers take pictures and study Martian rocks.

questions.q: What is a shooting star really?
o: A bit of rock burning up
questions.fact: Most shooting stars are no bigger than a grain of sand or a pebble.

questions.q: When can we see the stars best?
questions.fact: Stars show up best when the sky is really dark.

questions.q: What does a rocket do?
questions.fact: Rockets have to go about 17,500 miles per hour to orbit Earth.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.fact: A year on Mercury is only 88 Earth days long.

questions.q: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.fact: Pluto is now called a dwarf planet.

questions.q: Which planet is the biggest?
questions.fact: Jupiter has a giant storm, the Great Red Spot, that has lasted for well over a hundred years.

questions.q: What is the name of our galaxy?
questions.fact: The Milky Way has hundreds of billions of stars.

questions.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.fact: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon in 1969.

questions.q: What force keeps us on the ground?
questions.fact: On the Moon gravity is about one sixth as strong, so you could jump much higher.

questions.q: Which planet is the hottest?
questions.fact: Venus is hotter than Mercury because its thick air traps heat.

questions.q: What made the bowl-shaped craters on the Moon?
questions.fact: Some Moon craters are billions of years old.

questions.q: How long does Earth take to go around the Sun once?
questions.fact: Earth zooms around the Sun at about 67,000 miles per hour.

questions.q: Which planet spins on its side?
questions.fact: Uranus is tilted so far that it seems to roll around the Sun.

questions.q: What do we call the path a planet takes around the Sun?
questions.fact: The Moon has an orbit around Earth, too.

questions.q: What is a group of stars that makes a picture in the sky?
questions.fact: The Big Dipper is part of the constellation Ursa Major, the Great Bear.

questions.q: What is a rock from space that lands on Earth called?
questions.fact: Most space rocks burn up long before they reach the ground.

questions.q: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.fact: The sunlight you see right now left the Sun about eight minutes ago.

questions.q: Which planet has the shortest day?
questions.fact: Jupiter spins once in about ten hours, even though it is huge.

questions.q: What does a light-year measure?
questions.fact: A light-year is about six trillion miles.

questions.q: What is the closest star to our Sun?
questions.fact: Light from Proxima Centauri takes over four years to reach us.

questions.q: Which planet has the tallest volcano in the solar system?
questions.fact: Olympus Mons on Mars is about two and a half times as tall as Mount Everest.

questions.q: What is the Sun mostly made of?
questions.fact: Deep inside, the Sun turns hydrogen into helium to make its energy.

questions.q: What was the first human-made satellite to orbit Earth?
questions.fact: Sputnik 1 launched in 1957 and beeped as it circled Earth.

questions.q: About how long does the Moon take to orbit Earth?
questions.fact: The Moon always shows us the same face.

questions.q: What was the name of the 1969 mission that landed people on the Moon?
questions.fact: The Apollo 11 crew were Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins.

questions.q: What causes the seasons on Earth?
o: Earth's tilt as it orbits the Sun
Earth getting closer to the Sun
questions.fact: Earth is actually a little closer to the Sun in January than in July.

questions.q: Which spacecraft launched in 1977 is now the farthest human-made object from Earth?
questions.fact: Voyager 1 is sending back signals from interstellar space.

questions.q: What has gravity so strong that not even light can escape?
questions.fact: Many black holes form when a giant star runs out of fuel and collapses.

questions.q: Which planet takes about 165 Earth years to orbit the Sun?
questions.fact: Neptune was found in 1846 using math before anyone spotted it in a telescope.

questions.q: What is the Hubble?
questions.fact: Hubble has been taking pictures from orbit since 1990.

questions.q: What is a nebula?
o: A cloud of gas and dust in space
questions.fact: New stars are born inside nebulae.
